subject: Post-call: Finlytics batching/concurrency & pricing recap
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Finlytics batching/concurrency & pricing recap

Hi Anita — thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned. I copied Marissa and Aditya for pricing and commercial follow-up.

Key takeaways from our discovery:
- Current target workload: ~10M tokens/day (roughly 300M tokens/month) with steady daytime traffic and predictable nightly troughs.
- Typical request profile: user prompts ~120 tokens in, model outputs ~80 tokens on average (so ~200 tokens total per request).
- Concurrency: expected sustained concurrency ~6-10 concurrent requests during peak; peak spikes up to ~18 for short windows.
- Batching expectations: this is a streaming-heavy integration with continuous batching enabled server-side. You expect us to take advantage of continuous batching windows (~50-200ms) to reduce unit cost without harming tail latency.
- SLOs: target P50 latency <250ms, P95 <600ms for the user-facing calls.

Cost and budget signals you shared:
- Target unit economics: looking for a target of ~$35 per 1M tokens (customer target).
- Monthly budget range: preliminary budget range $25k–$60k/month depending on pilot terms and discounts.

Open questions / asks for you to confirm:
1) Can you confirm the 300M tokens/month estimate (monthly average) vs. any seasonal spikes?
2) Do you have any hard constraints on P95 tail latency for the user flows?
3) Any procurement timelines or specific contract terms we should know about (SOC2 evidence, data residency)?

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll send a usage template (attached) for you to fill in detailed per-route token estimates (finlytics_usage_template.csv).
- Marissa/Aditya will follow up with an initial commercial/discount structure and a couple of options: hosted usage vs. reserved/dedicated capacity.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week with one of our infra engineers to validate continuous batching assumptions and expected tail latencies.

Attachments: finlytics_usage_template.csv (blank usage template)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed times for next week.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finlytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-03-28T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finlytics batching/concurrency & pricing recap

Thanks Camila — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming ~300M tokens/month average; we see 3x monthly seasonality on marketing-driven days but those are predictable and short (2-3 days).
- Target unit price: yes, our internal target is ~$35 / 1M tokens for the steady-state workload. We can entertain a higher pilot price if there’s a clear path to that target with committed volume.
- Continuous batching: we expect continuous batching on your side; our main concern is tail latency for the user flows (P95 ideally <700ms end-to-end).
- Procurement: procurement is targeting a July go-live for production. They’ll need SOC2 docs and standard NDA/PO process.

Can you send a sample estimate for both hosted usage (no commit) and a reserved capacity option (6-12 month commit)? Also please include estimated unit economics showing how batching + reserved capacity changes the $/1M tokens.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30m call if you want to walk through the usage template once we populate it.

—
Anita Shah
Head of ML Products, Finlytics
anita.shah@finlytics.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Finlytics batching/concurrency & pricing recap

Forwarding Anita’s response — procurement timeline = July go-live, target $35/1M, monthly avg 300M tokens, some short predictable spikes.

Internal notes / asks:
- Marissa: can you put together a 2-option commercial (hosted vs reserved) showing list and discounted unit price to hit ~$35 with an illustrative commit (e.g., 300M/month for 6 months)? Attached a quick calc I started (prelim_pricing_calc.xlsx).
- Aditya: please include a short note on tail latency impact from continuous batching and whether we should recommend any request-level changes on Finlytics’ side to keep P95 under 700ms.

I think we should propose a pilot structure: 3-month pilot (no heavy penalty) with a 6-month committed follow-on that reaches the $35 target. If reserved capacity is required to reach lower unit economics, show the $/1M at 0% discount, 20% and 40% discount tiers.

I’ll propose times for the technical deep-dive next week (include Ethan from infra).

—
Camila
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Finlytics batching/concurrency & pricing recap

Thanks Camila — notes below and attaching a cleaned pricing model (pricing_model_v2.xlsx).

High-level commercial proposals (illustrative):
Option A — Hosted (no commit)
- List: $90 / 1M tokens
- Discounted: first 3 months pilot at $65 / 1M (intro pilot rate)
- Notes: continuous batching yields material unit cost reduction but hosted is still higher due to burst risk and multi-tenant overhead.

Option B — Reserved / Dedicated Pool (commit)
- List baseline: $55 / 1M tokens
- With 6-month commit (300M/month avg): we can go to $35 / 1M (meets customer target)
- With 12-month heavier commit: could reach $28 / 1M

Unit economics and assumptions (short):
- Baseline hardware + ops unit cost (est): ~$12-18 / 1M tokens depending on effective batching.
- Continuous batching assumption: effective batching window ~50-200ms; for Finlytics profile (200 tokens/request) we estimate batching cuts marginal cost by ~25-45% compared to no-batching path.
- Tail latency impact: continuous batching adds minimal median latency but can increase P95 by ~50-150ms depending on traffic shaping; Ethan — please validate with infra whether we can keep P95 <700ms with the expected concurrency.

Recommended next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive (30-45m) with Ethan and Aditya to validate batching windows and real P95 projections.
2) Camila to collect completed usage template from Anita.
3) Draft an MOA with pilot terms (3-month pilot, definable commit to convert).

If we can get a 6-month commit at ~300M/month, Option B achieves their $35 target. I’ll prepare a short slide to show the math.

Attachments: pricing_model_v2.xlsx

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0127
